Generated source SHALL record generator artifact digest, declared inputs, output path identity, and source map.
Stage-0 is a strict syntactic and semantic subset of Edition 1; every Stage-0 source parses and has identical observations under Edition 1.

Stage-0 includes UTF-8/ASCII identifiers, modules, structs/enums, fixed integers/bool/byte, arrays/slices, functions, generics without specialization, Result/Option, ownership/borrows, explicit effects, unsafe raw memory, and freestanding/native code generation.
Stage-0 excludes macros, runtime reflection, async, managed domains, dynamic typing, relations, decimal, scalable vectors/tensors, profile libraries, and user-defined effect handlers.
Stage-0 grammar is generated by disabling named Edition 1 productions, not maintained as an unrelated grammar.
Stage-0 uses the same checked arithmetic, evaluation order, initialization/drop, panic-abort policy, provenance, and C/omni_v1 ABI subset.
The seed compiler consumes canonical Stage-0 source and emits one reference object format/ISA plus deterministic diagnostic records.
Every Stage-0 restriction is represented by a feature predicate and tested against the Edition 1 parser/model to prove subset inclusion.
A canonical target identity is `arch-vendor-os-environment-abi[data-model]+feature-set`, with lowercase registered components and sorted feature names.
Aliases resolve through the signed target registry to exactly one canonical identity and cannot depend on the host machine.

Target manifests declare byte order, scalar widths/alignments, pointer widths per address space, maximum object size, stack alignment, atomic widths/lock-freedom, vector model, object format, ABI supplement, unwind/debug formats, and feature detection method.
Baseline feature sets are explicit. A distribution artifact cannot execute an instruction outside its baseline except within a correctly guarded multiversioned body.
Runtime feature detection is trusted only through the OS/firmware mechanism named by the target manifest; unprivileged self-reporting may further narrow but not widen authorized features.
Feature dispatch chooses a body whose required feature set is a subset of detected and deployment-policy-authorized features. Selection is cached with thread-safe initialization.

Target-specific semantics are limited to implementation-defined data layout, ABI/platform facilities, conditional instructions, and classified hardware faults. Core expression meaning remains unchanged.
Unsupported target features produce translation rejection or `TargetFeatureFault` before entering the body; illegal instruction traps are not an acceptable dispatch mechanism in safe hosted code.
Address spaces are registered with width, representation, accessibility, coherence, atomicity, provenance recovery, and conversion rules.
Every normative clause that admits more than one observable result SHALL classify the choice using exactly one term from this document.
Implementation-defined choices SHALL appear in the implementation manifest and artifact fingerprint when they can affect linking, layout, execution, persistence, or diagnostics.
Unspecified choices SHALL be finite and explicitly enumerated; unconstrained behavior is prohibited.
Quality-of-implementation latitude MAY affect performance, diagnostic wording beyond required fields, code layout, and other non-observable details.
An erroneous program SHALL not produce a conforming release artifact, although tools MAY construct recovery trees for editing.
A resource failure SHALL be reported through the allocator/API result, artifact fault policy, or target-mandated abort path named by the applicable rule.
An external hardware failure does not make prior safe behavior invalid; target supplements SHALL classify its delivered signal, trap, abort, or environmental result.

Timing, power, electromagnetic leakage, cache state, and speculative microarchitectural state are not ordinary core observations; constant-time and hardened profiles add explicit security observations.
Type identity is nominal for structs, enums, traits, opaque types, capabilities, effects, and aliases declared `distinct`; ordinary `type` aliases are transparent.
Tuples, function types, references, raw pointers, arrays, slices, and generic instantiations are structurally equal when all constituents and qualifiers are equal.
Recursive nominal types require an indirection, unsized tail, managed reference, or opaque boundary; infinitely sized value types are erroneous.
Every safe value satisfies its type validity invariant. Invalid scalar bit patterns cannot be constructed or observed in safe code.
`bool` has values `false` and `true`; `char` is any Unicode scalar; references are non-null, aligned, live, and provenance-valid; enums have a declared live variant.
Zero-sized types occupy no logical bytes but have distinct ownership/drop events. Arrays of zero-sized types retain length and iteration count.
`Never` is uninhabited and coerces to any type. Diverging expressions have type `Never`.
Unsized types are `[T]`, `str`, `dyn Trait`, and declared extern types. They may occur only behind a pointer/reference/owner or as the final field of a declared dynamically sized aggregate.
Public functions, public fields, FFI declarations, persisted schemas, capabilities, and exported constants require explicit types and effects.
Inference is local to a function/item body and must have a unique principal solution after defaults. Ambiguity is a diagnostic, not arbitrary selection.
Generic parameter kinds are type, lifetime, const value, effect row, and capability type. Defaults may reference earlier parameters only.
Constraint solving normalizes aliases and associated types, applies coherence-selected implementations, and terminates under the edition solver restrictions.
Trait objects contain only object-safe traits: no methods requiring `Self: Sized`, no generic methods, and associated types/consts required by calls must be fixed.
Downcast identity uses a 128-bit stable type fingerprint only for types opting into runtime identity; ordinary private type identity is not serialized.
Specialization exists only inside a sealed specialization family with a strict partial order where each pair of applicable implementations has one unique greatest element.

Implicit coercions are limited to lifetime shortening, `&mut T` to `&T`, reborrow, array reference to slice reference, concrete reference/owner to object-safe trait object, function item to function pointer, noncapturing closure to compatible function pointer, unsizing, and `Never` to any type.
No implicit numeric conversion, allocation, cloning, reference-count change, dynamic boxing, blocking, or capability acquisition occurs as a coercion.

Refinements are conjunctions of linear integer bounds, equalities, finite-set membership, length/alignment/unit predicates, and sealed protocol-state predicates. Undischarged obligations require explicit runtime checks or proof parameters.
Units and dimensions normalize to a rational scale and integer exponent vector. Unit metadata is erased from native ABI only after conversion is explicit and overflow-checked.
`Dynamic` is an explicit boxed tagged value with runtime type identity, checked extraction, `dynamic` effect for reflective operations, and no implicit conversion to static types.
`unsafe` permits performing operations with programmer-proved preconditions; it does not disable ordinary typing, ownership, effect, capability, initialization, or control-flow checks.
Unsafe operations are legal only inside an `unsafe` block/function or through an unsafe trait implementation, and their unsafe effect is visible in MIR and audit reports.
Calling an unsafe function requires an unsafe context even when the caller can prove its preconditions; safe wrappers discharge and document the proof.
Each unsafe operation has a named obligation record with precondition, protected invariant, permitted optimizer assumptions, and failure containment class.

If an unsafe precondition is false at event `e`, that execution becomes invalid from `e` onward. Observations before `e` remain required. Other executions and paths not reaching `e` retain full semantics.

An optimizer may assume an unsafe precondition only on paths that reach the operation and only while the facts/objects on which it depends remain live. Assumption provenance SHALL point to the obligation.

Invalid unsafe execution does not authorize compile-time compromise, cross-process effects, or modification of immutable artifacts; such outcomes are outside the language model and addressed by hardening.

Raw allocation requires `(size, alignment, address-space, allocator-family)` and returns a provenance-bearing allocation handle or failure. Zero-size allocations use a non-dereferenceable aligned sentinel or a declared unique object.
Deallocation requires the original live allocation identity, compatible allocator family, exact or accepted layout, no live derived references, and no outstanding device/foreign ownership.
Raw dereference requires live allocation provenance, in-bounds access, alignment unless using unaligned operations, valid address space, permissions, and a valid value for typed reads.

Inline assembly declares target, feature predicates, inputs, outputs, late outputs, clobbered registers, flags, memory regions, stack behavior, unwind behavior, control-flow successors, and volatility.
Assembly marked `pure`/`nomem`/`readonly` is verified syntactically where possible and remains an unsafe promise. Omitted memory clobbers cannot be inferred.

Assembly may branch only to declared labels, may unwind only with an explicit compatible unwind contract, and may not silently alter stack pointer, capability registers, TLS, or reserved runtime registers.
MMIO values use volatile device operations at declared widths and endianness. Ordinary references to MMIO storage are prohibited.

DMA registration pins or otherwise stabilizes buffers, establishes device-visible address mapping, records direction/coherence, and transfers a typed DMA lease. CPU access while leased follows the lease contract.
Device reset/revocation invalidates DMA leases atomically from the provider perspective; cleanup must tolerate completion/reset races without reusing storage early.
Update metadata uses separately scoped root, timestamp, snapshot, targets, delegation, revocation, and advisory roles with threshold signatures and expiration.
Root metadata is versioned and updated only through a chain validated from a trusted root with rollback protection.
Timestamp metadata prevents freeze and detects stale snapshots. Snapshot metadata binds exact versions/hashes of delegated metadata and prevents mix-and-match.
Target metadata binds package/artifact identity, version, length, digest, and custom compatibility fields, preventing wrong-package substitution.
Clients enforce monotonically nondecreasing metadata versions, expiration using an authorized clock or offline freshness policy, and maximum metadata/target sizes.
Endless-data defenses require declared length before download, streaming limits, decompression limits, and hash verification.
Revocation identifies exact content digests/keys/versions and effective time/severity. A security-revoked artifact is not selected or executed absent an audited emergency waiver.
Offline mirrors carry the complete signed metadata chain and checkpoints. Mirror transport cannot override signatures or freshness.
Newline MAY terminate a statement when the parser is at a complete statement boundary and the next token cannot continue the current expression or declaration.
A newline MUST NOT terminate a statement when the current construct is syntactically incomplete or the next token is a designated continuation token.
Continuation tokens include binary operators, `.`, `?.`, `?`, `??`, `,`, `)`, `]`, `}`, `::`, and other grammar-declared continuation forms. The complete set is normative.
Semicolons MAY be used explicitly and remain grammar separators; they are not required at ordinary statement boundaries when newline termination is unambiguous.
Formatter output MUST be canonical and MUST NOT rely on indentation alone to alter the semantic interpretation of an already valid expression.
Braced blocks remain valid in every context where the grammar admits blocks. Indentation-first formatting is preferred but does not create a second semantic language.

Release translation MUST reject source for which newline interpretation remains ambiguous after the continuation rules are applied. IDE recovery MAY construct recovery nodes, but those nodes remain non-translatable.
Wire/persistent schemas are independent of native layout and use stable schema, type, field, and variant identifiers.
Edition 1 canonical encoding begins with magic/version and encodes records as ascending numeric field ID, each with explicit wire type and length where applicable.
Unsigned integers use minimal unsigned LEB128; signed integers use minimal zigzag-LEB128 unless a fixed-width wire type is declared. Nonminimal encodings are rejected in canonical mode.
Fixed integers/floats are little-endian. Floating values use IEEE storage bits; canonical mode maps every NaN to one quiet canonical NaN per width and preserves signed zero.
Bytes and UTF-8 strings are length-prefixed. Strings are validated UTF-8. Collections have element count and each variable element has bounded length/structure.
Booleans encode as one byte 0 or 1; other values are rejected.
Record field IDs are unique. Duplicate singular fields are errors; repeated fields use an explicit repeated type. Unknown fields are skipped/preserved according to schema policy.
Variant IDs are stable integers. Unknown variants return a typed unknown-variant result or preserved opaque variant only when the schema declares extensibility.
Canonical ordering is ascending field ID, map entries sorted by canonical key bytes, and sets sorted by canonical element bytes. Duplicate canonical map/set keys are errors.
Compatibility classes are backward-readable, forward-readable, bidirectional, migration-required, and breaking. The schema checker computes class from declared changes.

Adding optional fields with defaults is backward-compatible; removing required fields, reusing IDs, changing wire type/meaning, narrowing ranges, or changing canonical defaults is breaking unless versioned migration is required.
Zero-copy views require alignment, endianness, lifetime ownership of the input buffer, validated bounds, and representation compatibility. Otherwise decoding copies/converts.
Decoders enforce schema-declared maximum nesting, total bytes, collection counts, string lengths, allocation budget, and processing fuel before allocating or recursing.
Hostile-input validation completes before constructing a safe value with invariants stronger than the wire representation.

Crash-safe persistent records use checksummed length-delimited frames and commit markers/journal protocol named by the persistence profile; partial frames are ignored/recovered, never interpreted as complete values.
